instructions: Rinse the rice. Put it in a small pot with 1 1/4 cups water, bring it to a boil, then turn the heat to low and cover. Cook for 15 minutes, then take it off the heat and leave it covered for 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, heat the oven to 400°F. Use 1 tbsp of the butter to grease a 2-quart baking dish. Cut the chicken into small bite-size pieces, slice the onion thin and trim and separate the mushrooms.

Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the chicken and cook for 4 to 5 minutes, stirring now and then, until it has lost its raw color. Add the onion and mushrooms and cook for 3 minutes, until soft. Try not to brown them, so the sauce stays white.
Add 2 tbsp of the butter and let it melt. Sprinkle in the flour and stir for 2 minutes.

Slowly pour in the milk, stirring the whole time. Simmer for 3 to 4 minutes, until the sauce is thick enough to coat the back of a spoon. Stir in 1 tsp salt and the pepper, then take the pan off the heat. Chicken thighs are best at 175°F in the middle; if you have a thermometer, check it there. No thermometer? Cut a piece open: it's done when there's no pink.
Stir the hot rice with the ketchup, 1/4 tsp salt and the last 1 tbsp butter until it's evenly orange-pink. Spread it in the baking dish.
Spoon the chicken and sauce over the rice. Scatter the mozzarella over the top.
Bake for 10 to 12 minutes, until the cheese has melted and the top is lightly browned.
Sprinkle the parsley over the top. Serve straight from the dish.
method_notes: Japanese Cooking 101 leads (5.0 from 1 vote, so a fallback; no chicken doria page has 20 ratings): ketchup-seasoned rice, a quick chicken and mushroom white sauce, and cheese baked on top for 10 minutes. Hiroko Liston and Japanese Taste show the same layers; Hiroko bakes the white sauce poured over rice, chicken and mushrooms mixed together. The rice here is 1 cup dry (about 3 cups cooked) so the dish feeds four, and the lead's white pepper is plain black pepper.
